vendor: Google (the scope); the assistant's vendor holds the token
product: An assistant connected to a personal Google Drive with drive.readonly
description: Any assistant a person connects to their own Drive with the read-only scope. Google classes drive.readonly as a restricted scope — "View and download all your Drive files" — and the per-file alternative, drive.file, reaches only files the user opened with the app. An assistant that searches needs the restricted one. The corpus it then searches defaults to the user corpus: files owned by or shared to the user.

reach_names.host: the Drive as a store: every file owned by or shared to the user
reach_names.tenant: the Google account the consent was given for

not_reachable.what: writing, moving, sharing or deleting files
not_reachable.why: drive.readonly is "View and download"; drive and drive.file are separate scopes and are not in this grant
a drive connector reaches a drive, not a disk

grant.note: drives hold exported keys, service-account files, .env backups and password exports beside everything else. Reading all files reads those. Inferred, not documented.

grant.control: Google's consent screen; the assistant's vendor holds the refresh token
grant.note: the connector acts as the account holder

grant.control: the OAuth scope — restricted in Google's classification, so the assistant's vendor had to pass restricted-scope verification
grant.note: drive.readonly — "View and download all your Drive files." The default corpus of a listing is "files owned by or shared to the user"; whether shared drives are included is open, below.

sources.label: Drive API scopes and their classification

contradictions.advertised: "search your files" (the shape, as assistants describe it)
contradictions.permitted: drive.readonly over the user corpus; whether the assistant sets includeItemsFromAllDrives, and so whether shared drives are searched, is not stated on either page

research_needed.question: Are shared drives in the corpus the assistant searches, or only files owned by or shared to the user?
research_needed.how: The assistant vendor's connector page, or a listing from an account you are entitled to run, against the Drive API's corpora definition.

research_needed.question: Does the assistant download and retain file content, or read on demand? Restricted-scope data stored on servers carries Google's own conditions.
research_needed.how: The vendor's data-retention page and Google's restricted-scope requirements, quoted.

research_needed.question: Which assistants passed restricted-scope verification for drive.readonly, and which use drive.file (per-file) instead?
research_needed.how: Each vendor's consent screen names its scopes; read them from the screen, do not connect.
